title: RBI: Circular — Non-Resident Deposits - Comprehensive Single Return (NRD-CSR)(R012): Submission under CIMS Sankalan Portal
applicability: Banks maintaining Non-Resident Deposits (NRD) Accounts
description: RBI has issued a circular concerning Non-Resident Deposits - Comprehensive Single Return (NRD-CSR)(R012): Submission under CIMS Sankalan Portal.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India transitioned the Non-Resident Deposits - Comprehensive Single Return (NRD-CSR) reporting to the Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) Sankalan portal, assigning it the return code R012 and rationalising its formats for bank-wise consolidated data. This circular was issued in supersession of A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 19 dated August 07, 2013, to update reporting channels and administrative management of user access. In practice, the nodal office of banks must now submit the NRD-CSR (R012) report through one of three specific channels: system-to-system integration, file upload on the data portal, or a screen-based web form on the data collection portal.
takeaway: Submit the NRD-CSR (R012) report on or before the 10th of the month following the month to which the NRD data pertains using one of the three permitted channels on the CIMS Sankalan portal.

The NRD-CSR (R012) return can be submitted to RBI on CIMS through one of the three channels mentioned below: System-to-system integration: The returns will be collected directly from the reporting entities’ ADF server to RBI CIMS server. File upload on Data Portal: Reporting entities can login to CIMS Data collection portal, upload and submit the return specific file. Screen based web form on Data Collection Portal: Reporting entities can login to CIMS data collection portal and key in return specific information in the web form created for the return.
takeaway: The NRD-CSR report may be submitted on or before 10th of the month following the month to which the NRD data pertains.

title: RBI: Amendment — Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026
applicability: Mutual funds registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, pension funds registered with the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, and insurance companies registered with the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India that do not belong to the promoter group of the investee banking company, as well as portfolio managers and local area banking companies.
description: RBI has issued a amendment concerning Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has introduced the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026, which allow qualifying mutual funds, pension funds, and insurance companies to seek a one-time approval for subsequent major shareholding acquisitions up to 10 percent. This change was based on a review to streamline the approval process for specific institutional investors while maintaining regulatory oversight. In practice, qualifying persons must now submit applications through PRAVAAH along with Form A, banking companies must furnish comments in Form A1, and major shareholders with one-time approval must report holdings crossing below or above five percent within three working days.
takeaway: Submit applications for one-time approval through PRAVAAH along with the declaration in Form A, and ensure that any decrease or increase of the aggregate holding to below or above five percent of total paid-up share capital or voting rights is reported to the Reserve Bank and the concerned banking company within three working days.

title: RBI: Amendment — Payments Banks Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights Directions
applicability: Mutual funds registered with SEBI, pension funds registered with PFRDA, and insurance companies registered with IRDAI qualifying as a 'qualifying person' or 'qualifying person with one-time approval' under the directions, as well as banking companies, portfolio managers, and banks applying on behalf of qualifying persons belonging to the promoter group or group of the bank.
description: RBI has issued a amendment concerning Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has introduced the Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026, which modify the Master Direction of 2025 by permitting mutual funds, insurance companies, and pension funds to obtain a one-time approval for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding up to 10 percent. This change was based on a review to streamline shareholding acquisition rules for institutional investors while maintaining regulatory oversight. In practice, qualifying entities seeking one-time approval must now submit applications through PRAVAAH with Form A or Form A1, banks must furnish comments accordingly, and entities with one-time approval must report holding decreases or increases across the five percent threshold to the RBI and the banking company within three working days.
takeaway: Submit applications for one-time approval through PRAVAAH along with Form A declarations, ensure banking companies furnish comments in Form A1, and report any decrease or increase of aggregate holdings crossing the five percent threshold to the Reserve Bank and the banking company within three working days.

title: IBBI: Circular — Judgments of Hon'ble High Courts on Cessation of Interim Moratorium in Respect of Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors
applicability: Registered Insolvency Professionals, Recognised Insolvency Professional Entities, and Registered Insolvency Professional Agencies
description: IBBI has issued a circular concerning judgments of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court and Delhi High Court on cessation of interim moratorium in respect of personal guarantors to corporate debtors.
summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026 inserted sub-section (4) in sections 96 and 124 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, providing that the interim moratorium shall not apply in respect of a personal guarantor to a corporate debtor with effect from May 26, 2026. This was issued following judgments from the Hon'ble Bombay High Court and Delhi High Court confirming that this retroactive provision applies to applications that were filed and pending before the Adjudicating Authority as of that date. In practice, compliance workflows and ongoing proceedings will treat the interim moratorium as having ceased to operate for pending applications as of May 26, 2026.
takeaway: Review active insolvency proceedings involving personal guarantors to corporate debtors to account for the cessation of the interim moratorium effective from May 26, 2026, for pending applications.
